claim: Visit Singapore publishes a self-guided Chinatown walking route covering Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple and Pagoda Street with map and MRT info.
quote: A self-guided Chinatown Singapore walking tour map features main attractions including temples, Pagoda Street, hawker centres, museums, and nearby MRT stations.

claim: The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is a five-storey Tang-dynasty-style complex built in 2007, open daily 9am-6pm with free admission.
quote: The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is a five-storey Tang-dynasty-style complex housing what is believed to be a sacred tooth relic of the Gautama Buddha, built in 2007 and funded by donations from the Singapore Buddhist community.

claim: Thian Hock Keng on Telok Ayer Street is Singapore's oldest Chinese temple, built 1839-42 without nails and dedicated to sea-goddess Mazu.
quote: Thian Hock Keng is Singapore's oldest Chinese temple, located in the heart of Chinatown with rich history and cultural significance. The temple, which means 'Temple of Heavenly Happiness,' dates back to the 1800s and is dedicated to Mazu, a Chinese sea goddess.

claim: The former House of Tan Teng Niah (1900) is the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India, now a brightly-painted heritage photo stop on Kerbau Road.
quote: Built in 1900, the former house of Tan Teng Niah is the last surviving Chinese villa in Little India. Tan Teng Niah was a towkay (Chinese businessman of good standing) who owned several sweet-making factories along Serangoon Road that used sugarcane to produce sweets.

claim: The Indian Heritage Centre on Campbell Lane is open Tue-Sun 10am-6pm with last admission 5:30pm, closed Mondays including public holidays.
quote: Tuesday – Sunday, 10am to 6pm (Last admission at 5:30pm). The centre is closed every Monday, including public holidays which fall on Monday unless otherwise stated.

claim: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple, established 1855, opens daily 5.30am-noon and 4-9pm with a midday closure 12:15-4pm; shoes must be removed.
quote: The opening hours are Mon–Sun 5.30am–noon, 4–9pm. The temple is closed between 12:15 and 4 pm... established in 1855, making it one of Singapore's oldest houses of worship.

claim: The Malay Heritage Centre at Istana Kampong Glam has reopened after its extensive revamp; permanent galleries run Tue-Sun 10am-6pm and the compound 8am-9pm.
quote: After an extensive revamp and restoration, we are so glad to finally have our doors open again. Permanent Galleries: Tuesday–Sunday, 10am–6pm (closed Mondays); Compound: Tuesday–Sunday, 8am–9pm.

claim: Haji Lane is a 250m strip of shophouses packed with indie boutiques, cafes, murals and bars; named indie stores include RE.DRMG, VINTAGEWKND, PLOP APPARELS, Wicked Laundry and Matter Prints.
quote: Haji Lane is a 250-metre strip of shophouses in Kampong Glam — indie boutiques, specialty cafes, street murals, and bars all packed into one narrow alley... indie boutiques like RE.DRMG, VINTAGEWKND, and PLOP APPARELS.

claim: Sultan Mosque sits at 3 Muscat Street; the original 1824 building was demolished and the current dome-and-minaret structure was completed in 1932.
quote: The Sultan Mosque is located at 3 Muscat Street and is the focal point of the historic Kampong Glam area. The original structure was demolished about a century after the mosque was first built in 1824 to make way for the current building, which was completed in 1932.

claim: Tiong Bahru's Streamline Moderne walk-up flats (Singapore's first public housing, 1930s) cluster around Seng Poh Road, Yong Siak Street, Moh Guan Terrace and Tiong Poh Road with curved corners and horizontal lines suited to the tropics.
quote: The core of the estate — concentrated around Seng Poh Road, Yong Siak Street, Moh Guan Terrace, and Tiong Poh Road — is a remarkably intact collection of Streamline Moderne residential blocks from the 1930s... favouring horizontal lines, curved corners, and aerodynamic forms designed for tropical ventilation.

claim: Tiong Bahru Bakery on Eng Hoon Street is famed for its kouign-amann and croissants; nearby Cat Socrates at 78 Yong Siak Street stocks local books, Peranakan tiles and indie crafts after BooksActually moved online in 2022.
quote: Tiong Bahru Bakery on Eng Hoon Street — serving croissants that people consistently describe as the best in Singapore... Cat Socrates at 78 Yong Siak Street is one of the most beloved independent shops in Singapore — a browsing paradise of local books, Singaporean design pieces, Peranakan tiles, quirky homewares, and indie crafts.

claim: Koon Seng Road's pastel Peranakan shophouses are a roughly 50m stretch and Katong/Joo Chiat was Singapore's first Heritage Town (2011), with facades legally protected from alteration.
quote: At the intersection with Koon Seng Road, you'll step into one of Singapore's most iconic streets, lined with Peranakan shophouses. Though it's only around 50 metres long... The area was designated a national heritage conservation area in 1993 and named Singapore's first Heritage Town in 2011.

claim: The Katong Antique House is a private Peranakan museum-shophouse founded by the late Peter Wee, a 4th-generation Peranakan, and now run by Angeline Kong and Eric Ang.
quote: The Katong Antique House was owned by the late Peter Wee, a 4th generation Peranakan and former president of The Peranakan Association Singapore... The museum is currently led by Angeline Kong and Eric Ang.

claim: The Katong laksa rivalry pits 328 Katong Laksa (creamy, seafood-heavy, founded 1998 after taking over Marine Parade Laksa's premises) against Janggut/Marine Parade Laksa (lighter broth, more laksa-leaf), tracing back to a 1998 rent dispute.
quote: Mrs Teo, the landlady of 49 East Coast Road, decided to cash in on the success of Marine Parade Laksa and put her rental prices up in 1998, forcing the Ng brothers to move out. The premises were taken over by Nancy Lim (now Nancy Koh), who re-named the coffee shop 328 Laksa.

claim: Free walking tours in Singapore are either tip-based group walks (SGD 15-30 tip suggested) or genuinely free National Heritage Board self-guided trails, covering Chinatown, Little India, Kampong Glam, Tiong Bahru and the Civic District.
quote: Tip-based free tours are led by local guides who walk you through a neighbourhood for no upfront fee, with visitors typically tipping SGD $15–$30 per person. Additionally, self-guided free tours are genuinely zero-cost, where you follow a heritage trail map provided by the Singapore Tourism Board.

claim: Chinatown free walking tours typically start at Telok Ayer MRT and include Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple (Singapore's oldest Hindu shrine, 1827) and Fuk Tak Chi Museum.
quote: Tours starting at Telok Ayer MRT unpack the history of Chinese immigrants, with stops including Buddha Tooth Relic Temple, Sri Mariamman Temple (Singapore's oldest Hindu shrine, built in 1827), and the Fuk Tak Chi Museum.
